taxonomy.note: Older field guides and nursery sources may still use the former genus Gaura; preserve those names as synonyms but use current Oenothera placement canonically.

evidence: Hays — project Hays-local source pool contains 7 wild/noncultivated observations and flags the species as Hays Local; this is supporting occurrence evidence rather than a herbarium voucher.
Travis — UT Plant Resources Center Travis County herbarium index includes Gaura parviflora, the homotypic synonym of Oenothera curtiflora.
Williamson — UT Plant Resources Center Vascular Plants of Williamson County provides a detailed treatment under the accepted name Oenothera curtiflora.
target_zone_range.guardrail: No county occurrence inferred from statewide native status; named counties are supported by explicit local/herbarium/project occurrence evidence.

morphology.look_here_first: Look for the mismatch between plant size and flower size: a tall, densely velveteen annual carries a long crowded wand of extremely tiny flowers—only about 3 mm across.
diagnostic_traits: annual or biennial, taprooted, not rosetted at flowering
foliage and stems densely soft/velveteen hairy with glandular hairs
4 tiny white petals aging light rose
narrow hard indehiscent fruit around 8 mm long

confusers.separator: Both are annual former-gauras. O. curtiflora is much more densely velveteen and its flowers are tiny (~3 mm); O. suffulta has 12–19 mm white flowers, a largely glabrous inflorescence, and a short chunky 4-lobed fruit.
O. lindheimeri is a showy perennial with much larger flowers and an airy arching habit; O. curtiflora is a hairy annual with minute flowers.
